A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT-based Synthesizer work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on four benchmarks with seven policy models, alongside ablations, scaling experiments, and candidate-response analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments ablating LLM Repair and repeated Response LLM sampling.

M1.justification: Candidate generation, CoT analysis and synthesis, data filtering and repair, SFT training, and iterative grouping remain unchanged. Appendix D explains existing model roles; the revised repair wording does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and WikiTQ and evaluate GSM8k, MATH500, WikiTQ, and FeTaQA. Replacing MATH with MATH500 in several passages clarifies existing coverage: v1 already identifies MATH500 in Section 5.1 and lists 500 test examples.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain CoT-prompting, SC, USC, LMCOR, ArmoRM, and Scalar RM in their corresponding experiments. The new appendix bullet for CoT-prompting describes an existing baseline; Table 4 adds component ablations rather than new baseline methods.

E3.justification: The added ablations introduce training conditions without repair or repeated Response LLM sampling, producing 245k and 9k training examples respectively, versus the stated 295k full dataset. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, model configurations, and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B and Table 4 test the contributions of LLM Repair and repeated Response LLM sampling on GSM8k and MATH500 across seven policy models. This extends the existing component analyses; the earlier CoT/training ablations, scaling studies, correctness breakdown, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging was already stated in v1 Appendix B.3 and remains in v2 Appendix C.3; v2 also repeats it in the main text. Neither version reports dispersion or significance tests. Table 4's signed annotations represent accuracy differences, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New Table 4 reports average accuracies of 89.3/89.0/88.3 on GSM8k and 62.6/61.7/61.1 on MATH500 for full synthesis/without repair/without multiple responses. Section 5.2 also removes v1's misplaced claim of a 9.6-point GLM-4-Plus gain on GSM8k; Table 1 implies 2.8 points.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and generation-probability equation remain unchanged, with no added mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs. Appendix D's model definitions are explanatory descriptions of existing roles rather than new mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: synthesizing answers from potentially incorrect candidates, generating training data automatically, and enabling smaller synthesizers to improve larger policy models. MATH500 labeling clarifies the existing evaluation rather than changing claim scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 expands the explanation of resistance to repeated training instructions through diverse candidates and reasoning chains. Appendix B attributes differing ablation effects to training-data volume. New efficiency arguments compare five synthesis candidates with more than ten for SC and qualify the overhead discussion, without adding direct cost measurements.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the ablations' 245k and 9k training-set sizes and clarifies that scaling subsets are sampled separately from each method's training data. Main training-set sizes were already documented in v1. Hardware, optimization settings, prompts, and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. However, Appendix C.2 adds explicit positioning of single-pass synthesis against iterative refinement, debate, and decomposition/retrieval approaches, while Section 5.1 clarifies the distinction from LMCOR's training targets.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several experimental paragraphs, clarifies model terminology and benchmark names, adds acknowledgments and a model-role appendix, and adjusts appendix organization. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ablation display as Table 4, relocates Table 3 and appendix tables, and updates some captions and labels to MATH500. Existing diagrams, scaling plots, and case-study displays are retained, with limited formatting and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 provides additional evidence for the data-generation pipeline through repair and sampling ablations, improves explanations of model roles, and clarifies benchmark labeling. These are useful but limited gains: the ablations also change training-data volume, limiting component-specific conclusions, and the added efficiency arguments lack direct timing or compute measurements. The main empirical results and central method remain unchanged.
